# From Deployment to Routine Science: Webb’s Six-Month Commissioning

Webb was too large in its operational configuration to fit inside the available rocket’s Ariane 5 fairing, so it was designed to fold for launch. Unfolding involved more than 50 major steps and over 300 possible single points of failure. Any one could have diminished or crippled the mission, and repair would not have been possible at Webb’s distance from Earth.

Deployment proceeded smoothly. By the telescope’s second week, its secondary mirror and both primary-mirror wings had unfolded and latched, completing its fully deployed operational configuration. But deployment was only one stage on the way to routine science. During the first month, the telescope and instruments cooled for several weeks. Mirror alignment took place in months two through four, followed by instrument-mode calibration in months five and six. Webb began routine science operations after the six-month commissioning period.
